guidance: A planning count only. It does not say what your household should eat, and it is not nutrition, medical or food-safety advice. The calories per person per day figure is yours to set; the 2,000 default is a general nutrition guide, not a personal requirement. Special diets, allergies, infants, pregnancy, illness and pets are not modelled, stored food is assumed edible and in date, and package sizes are generic meal counts rather than product specifications. Ready.gov advises at least a several-day supply of non-perishable food as a starting point.
method: Person-days are people x days, and the calories to store are person-days x the chosen calories per person per day. The meals to plan are person-days x meals per person per day, so the average calories per meal is the total calories divided by the total meals. Days of food on hand describe how many days this household could already eat, so the food on hand is that many days x people person-days, converted to calories at the same daily figure; days covered is the smaller of that figure and the plan length, and the shortfall is the requirement less what is on hand. Outstanding meals are the shortfall in calories divided by the average meal, and each package row divides that meal count by the package size (6, 12, 24 or 48 meals) and rounds up to a whole package, so the meals supplied exceed the shortfall except where it divides exactly. A plan that is already covered shows zero packages. Inputs are a whole headcount from 1 to 12, a whole day count from 1 to 30, a whole calorie figure from 1,000 to 4,000 per person per day, whole meals from 2 to 5 per person per day and days of food on hand from 0 to 30 with at most one decimal. Everything runs in the browser with no uploads, storage or network calls, and the page stores nothing between visits.
